blocks.content: Unlike running water or wind, glaciers transport unsorted rock material ranging from fine rock flour to giant angular boulders without any hydraulic sorting.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Glaciers act as massive natural conveyor belts, transporting debris ranging from fine rock flour to huge boulders.
Glacial load is categorized into supraglacial (surface debris), englacial (internal load), and subglacial (bed load) transport.
Unlike water or wind, glacial transportation does not sort material by size, producing poorly sorted sediment known as glacial till.
Glacial erratics are large boulders transported far from their source and deposited onto bedrock of completely different composition.
Medial moraines are created when two converging valley glaciers merge their adjacent lateral moraines together.
Glacial till is unsorted and unstratified, whereas fluvio-glacial outwash deposits are sorted and stratified.
Medial moraines form specifically at the confluence of two valley glaciers combining their inner lateral moraines.
Glacial erratics serve as critical indicators for geologists to trace the exact direction of historic ice sheet movements.
